scope: General botanical and agronomic knowledge about each species. It is NOT inferred from the uploaded image: the app identifies the flower species (when the species is AI-supported), and this record describes that species in general. Flowering times are typical ranges and vary with cultivar, latitude, altitude and season - check local extension advice.
fruit_recognition: Pollinex does not detect or recognise fruit in images (no fruit model is trained). Fruit information below is reference knowledge about what the species produces after successful pollination and fertilisation.

apple.flower: Five-petalled flowers borne in clusters (usually 5-6 per spur); the central 'king' flower opens first.
apple.petals: Five, white to pink; buds are often deeper pink than the open flower.
apple.reproductive_structures: About 20 stamens with yellow anthers; five styles joined at the base over an inferior ovary.
apple.flowering: Blooms on spurs as leaves emerge; a single flower stays receptive for only a few days.
apple.flowering_period: Spring - roughly March-May in the temperate northern hemisphere; in India's hill states (e.g. Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir) mainly March-April, earlier at lower altitude.
apple.pollination_mechanism: Insect transfer of pollen from a compatible cultivar (cross-pollination).
apple.breeding_system: Mostly self-incompatible: orchards need a compatible pollinizer cultivar that flowers at the same time.

fruit.name: apple
fruit.characteristics: Fleshy fruit developing mainly from the floral tube around an inferior ovary; seeds in a five-chambered core. Poor pollination gives fewer seeds and misshapen or small fruit.

apple.agricultural_relevance: Major temperate fruit crop; fruit set depends on pollinizer placement, bee activity and weather during bloom.

peach.flower: Single or paired flowers on one-year-old shoots, often opening before the leaves.
peach.petals: Five, pink to deep pink; 'showy' cultivars have large petals, 'non-showy' cultivars small, cupped petals.
peach.reproductive_structures: Many stamens (about 20-30) around a single pistil with a superior ovary.
peach.flowering: Early bloom makes flowers vulnerable to spring frost.
peach.flowering_period: Late winter to early spring - roughly February-April in the temperate northern hemisphere; low-chill cultivars in subtropical regions flower earlier.
peach.pollination_mechanism: Mostly self-pollination within the flower; insects improve fruit set.
peach.breeding_system: Most commercial cultivars are self-compatible (self-fertile); a few are self-sterile and need a pollinizer.

fruit.name: peach
fruit.characteristics: Fleshy fruit with a single hard stone; skin usually downy (fuzzless in nectarines, the same species).

peach.agricultural_relevance: Important stone fruit; frost at bloom is a larger risk than lack of pollen.

pear.flower: Five-petalled flowers in clusters (corymbs) of about 5-8.
pear.reproductive_structures: About 20-30 stamens with distinctive red to purple anthers; usually five styles over an inferior ovary.
pear.flowering: Flowers produce nectar low in sugar, so bees may prefer other bloom nearby.
pear.flowering_period: Spring - usually slightly before or with apple bloom (roughly March-April in the temperate northern hemisphere).
pear.pollination_mechanism: Insect transfer of pollen from a compatible cultivar (cross-pollination).
pear.breeding_system: Most European pear cultivars are largely self-incompatible and need a compatible pollinizer.

fruit.name: pear
fruit.characteristics: Fleshy fruit with grit cells (stone cells) in the flesh and a seed core, like apple.

pear.agricultural_relevance: Temperate fruit crop; low bee attraction makes managed pollination and pollinizer planning important.

sunflower.flower: A composite head (capitulum): outer ray florets around hundreds to thousands of disc florets.
sunflower.petals: The yellow 'petals' are sterile ray florets; the fertile disc florets are small and tubular.
sunflower.reproductive_structures: Each disc floret is perfect: five anthers fused into a tube around the style (pollen is pushed out before the stigma opens - protandry).
sunflower.flowering: Disc florets open in rings from the edge of the head towards the centre over several days.
sunflower.flowering_period: Summer, a few months after sowing; in India grown in both kharif and rabi seasons, so timing depends on the sowing date.
sunflower.pollination_mechanism: Insect pollination between florets and heads; protandry reduces self-pollination within a floret.
sunflower.breeding_system: Wild types are largely self-incompatible; many modern hybrids are partly self-compatible but still yield better with bees.

fruit.name: sunflower 'seed'
fruit.characteristics: Each fertilised disc floret forms one dry fruit containing the oil-rich seed; unpollinated florets leave empty achenes.

sunflower.agricultural_relevance: Major oilseed and confectionery crop; seed set in the head centre is most sensitive to poor pollination.

hibiscus.flower: Large, solitary, showy flowers; each flower typically lasts about one day.
hibiscus.petals: Five (many more in double cultivars), in red, pink, orange, yellow or white.
hibiscus.reproductive_structures: A prominent staminal column: stamen filaments fused into a tube around the style, with anthers along it and five stigma lobes (pads) at the tip.
hibiscus.flowering: Flowers continuously on new growth in warm conditions.
hibiscus.flowering_period: Much of the year in tropical and subtropical climates (including most of India); seasonal or under glass in cooler regions.
hibiscus.pollination_mechanism: Animal transfer of pollen from the anthers to the five stigma pads.
hibiscus.breeding_system: Mostly grown as an ornamental and propagated by cuttings; many cultivars rarely set seed.

fruit.name: capsule
fruit.characteristics: When formed, a dry capsule that splits to release seeds. Hibiscus rosa-sinensis is not a fruit crop.

hibiscus.agricultural_relevance: Ornamental and hedge plant; flowers are also used culturally and in traditional preparations.

tomato.petals: Usually five or six yellow petals that curl back (reflex) when the flower is fully open.
tomato.reproductive_structures: Anthers fused into a yellow cone around the style; pollen is released inside the cone and shaken out by vibration.
tomato.flowering: Trusses open progressively up the plant over a long season.
tomato.flowering_period: Begins several weeks after transplanting; year-round in heated greenhouses, seasonal in the field.
tomato.pollination_mechanism: Vibration (buzz) pollination: shaking the flower releases pollen onto the stigma of the same flower.
tomato.breeding_system: Self-compatible and largely self-pollinating; greenhouses replace wind and insects with bumble bees or vibrating tools.

fruit.name: tomato
fruit.characteristics: Fleshy fruit with locules full of seeds in gel; poor pollination gives small, misshapen or seedless fruit.

tomato.agricultural_relevance: One of the most important vegetable crops; heat stress can make pollen non-viable even when flowers look ready.

strawberry.flower: Five-petalled flowers in small clusters (cymes); the primary flower opens first and produces the largest fruit.
strawberry.reproductive_structures: Many stamens (about 20-35) around a raised receptacle carrying hundreds of separate pistils.
strawberry.flowering: June-bearing cultivars flower once in spring; ever-bearing and day-neutral cultivars flower repeatedly.
strawberry.flowering_period: Mainly spring in temperate regions; in Indian plains and hills mostly late winter-spring, depending on cultivar and planting date.
strawberry.pollination_mechanism: Self-pollination plus wind and insects; every pistil must be pollinated for an evenly shaped fruit.
strawberry.breeding_system: Modern cultivars are largely self-fertile, but insect visits improve fruit size and shape.

fruit.name: strawberry
fruit.characteristics: The fleshy part is the swollen receptacle; the true fruits are the small achenes on the surface. Unpollinated pistils cause deformed fruit.

strawberry.agricultural_relevance: High-value berry crop, often grown in polytunnels or greenhouses where pollination must be managed.

brinjal.flower: Star-shaped flowers, solitary or in small clusters.
brinjal.petals: Five to six fused, pale to deep purple corolla lobes.
brinjal.reproductive_structures: Bright yellow anthers that open by terminal pores (poricidal) around the style; style length varies (long-, medium- and short-styled flowers).
brinjal.flowering: Long- and medium-styled flowers set fruit far more often than short-styled ones.
brinjal.flowering_period: Begins a few weeks after transplanting and continues through the season; grown year-round in much of India.
brinjal.pollination_mechanism: Mainly self-pollination aided by vibration; insects cause some cross-pollination.
brinjal.breeding_system: Self-compatible; often described as an often-cross-pollinated crop because insect cross-pollination occurs.

fruit.name: brinjal (eggplant, aubergine)
fruit.characteristics: Fleshy fruit, purple, green or white depending on cultivar, with many small seeds.

brinjal.agricultural_relevance: Major vegetable crop in South and South-East Asia; flower style type is a practical indicator of fruit set.

chilli.flower: Small flowers, usually solitary at the nodes.
chilli.petals: Usually five or six, white or greenish-white (purple in some cultivars).
chilli.reproductive_structures: Anthers often bluish to purple, splitting lengthwise to release pollen; the stigma is near or above the anthers.
chilli.flowering: Flowers open over a long season; high temperatures cause flower and fruit drop.
chilli.flowering_period: Begins several weeks after transplanting; in India grown in kharif, rabi and summer seasons depending on the region.
chilli.pollination_mechanism: Largely self-pollination; insects bring some cross-pollination.
chilli.breeding_system: Self-compatible; cross-pollination by insects can be substantial, so seed growers isolate cultivars.

fruit.name: chilli pepper
fruit.characteristics: Hollow fruit with seeds on a central placenta; pungency comes from capsaicinoids in the placental tissue.

chilli.agricultural_relevance: Important spice and vegetable crop; heat and humidity during flowering strongly affect fruit set.
